small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs targeting M=N_OUT (=128*126*126 ≈ 2M) which is huge: try BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_OC=128 with num_warps=8 stages=3/4, and BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_OC=256.
- BLOCK_K is rounded up to 128 for IC*KH*KW=72, wasting ~44% of K-flops; specialize on K_REAL=72 by using BLOCK_K=72 only if a power-of-two isn't required, or split into two stages (BLOCK_K=64 main + remainder=8) so the dot only processes real K.
- Reorder program IDs / add swizzling (group pid_n in tiles of 8) to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile, and ensure pid_oc is the fastest-moving axis for weight reuse across N.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM with output tile layout `(BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW)` per program instead of a flat N_OUT axis. Adjacent output pixels share input rows (KH×KW window overlap), so a spatial tile gives huge input reuse via shared memory / register reuse — the current flat indexing reloads overlapping input windows for every output.
- Use NHWC (channels-last) layout for input and output so the GEMM-K axis (IC×KH×KW) is contiguous in memory; this lets BLOCK_K loads coalesce and enables vectorized 128-bit reads. With IC=8 the K dim is tiny — loop over KH×KW outside and do a small inner GEMM on IC, accumulating across kernel taps.
- Consider a persistent-CTA / split-K-free kernel where each program owns a fixed (oc_tile, spatial_tile) and streams N=batch through it, amortizing weight loads (weight is only OC*IC*KH*KW = 64*72 = small, fits in registers/SMEM once).
